column2: req_desc

Sightline orbit and alignment readout
The sightline scene on each chapter page turns its camera between -60° and +60° by drag, by scroll inside the scene or by arrow keys, and shows the alignment percentage from Business rules both on screen and as the scene's aria-valuenow.

Sightline resolution
When the camera comes within the resolve window of the chapter's sightline, or the visitor uses Align, the title appears as a real heading, the readout locks at 100% in the accent colour, Enter chapter becomes enabled and the resolution is announced.

Resolved chapters saved to the path
A signed-in visitor who resolves and enters a chapter sees it marked resolved on the chapter index after a reload, and finds it recorded with their last position in their PocketBase saved path.

Static viewpoints without motion
With reduced motion requested, the Motion switch off, or no WebGL, each scene becomes a radio group of seven still viewpoints, and choosing the sightline viewpoint resolves the chapter exactly as alignment does.

Numeral morph on entry
Following a chapter link from the index or the rail morphs the chapter numeral into the chapter header within the time given in Motion and effects, and swaps it instantly under reduced motion.

Chapter scene layout per viewport
The scene is full-bleed at 375 and 768 pixels wide and framed at 1280 pixels, and the chapter rail is a bottom drawer, a top strip or a right-edge column at those widths, with no horizontal overflow.

Rule engine classifies live
Editing, adding or removing a rule in the chapter VI rule engine reclassifies the twelve seeded specimens in place by first-match order and announces the classified count.

Classifier measured on held-out points
In the chapter VII classifier, moving a training point or pressing Train retrains the published perceptron, updates held-out accuracy and confusion counts in place, and announces the result.

Word neighbours in context
In the chapter VIII exhibit, choosing a word and a context lists the three nearest words by the published similarity rule, updated in place and announced.

Spring sculpture regimes
In the chapter IV spring sculpture, changing stiffness or damping updates the named damping regime in place, and Pluck sets the sculpture oscillating to rest, or shows the rest pose at once without motion.

Keyboard-only exhibit walk
A visitor using only the keyboard can resolve a chapter, enter it, and operate every control of all four exhibits to reach each published result.

Index and timeline columns
The chapter index and the timeline archive show one column at 375, two at 768 and three at 1280 pixels wide, in the published reading order.

Timeline, search and sources
The timeline, search and sources endpoints and screens list only published items in the published order, and search results update as the visitor types.

Bookmarks
A signed-in visitor can bookmark and unbookmark chapters and timeline events, stored in PocketBase and listed on their account page.

Withdrawn items disappear
A withdrawn chapter or event disappears from the index, rail, timeline, search, bookmarks and saved paths, and its media links stop resolving, as qualified in Business rules.

Published empty and not-found copy
A chapter with no published events shows the published empty-state copy to visitors and curators, and unknown or withdrawn pages show the published not-found heading with status 404.

Phone walk with motion off
On a 375-pixel-wide phone with reduced motion, a visitor walks a chapter, resolves it by viewpoint and reaches every exhibit result by taps alone.

Registration and sign-in
Visitors register and sign in with accounts stored in PocketBase, and staff sign in with seeded accounts whose role decides what they may do.

Motion and sound preferences
The Motion and Sound switches take effect at once and persist for each signed-in visitor in PocketBase across reloads.

Accounts outage
When PocketBase is unreachable, including from boot, the app still starts, sign-in and path saving answer 503 with the published copy, and the exhibition stays browsable, as qualified in Server boundary.

Dialogs by keyboard
Every dialog and sheet keeps Tab and Shift+Tab inside itself, closes on Escape, and returns focus to the control that opened it, as qualified in Interactions for the booking dialog.

Sessions with server-decided status
Guided sessions show their status and seats left exactly as the server reports them, whatever the device clock says.

Booking closes 30 minutes before start
The server closes booking 30 minutes before a session starts, by its own clock, and rejects later bookings with 409 and the published copy.

One winner for the last seats
When simultaneous bookings ask for more seats than remain, only bookings that fit succeed, and every other one gets 409 with no Kill Bill charge.

Idempotent purchases
Every purchase, membership action, refund and session cancellation requires an Idempotency-Key, returns the stored response for a repeated key, returns the first result to a duplicate sent while that key is still in flight, and rejects a reused key sent with a different body.

Ticket settlement record
A settled ticket purchase leaves exactly one ledger row, one Kill Bill invoice and payment for seats times the catalog price, one ticket email and one PDF, and a failed purchase leaves no ledger row, email, PDF or successful Kill Bill payment.

Mail outage keeps the booking
When Mailpit is unreachable, a booking still succeeds with the published confirmation heading and the delayed-email banner, and its single email arrives once mail can be delivered, as qualified in Services.

Keyboard booking journey
A visitor using only the keyboard signs in, opens a session, books seats and reads the confirmation, and focus returns to that session afterwards.

Donations in exact minor units
A donation charges exactly the entered amount, in integer minor units of the chosen currency and within the published limits, and records a matching ledger row, Kill Bill payment, receipt email and PDF.

Private receipts
Receipt emails and PDFs show only the payer's own name, the item, the amount and currency, the date, the receipt number and the card's last four digits, and never notes, other people's details or provider identifiers.

Donation journey
A signed-in visitor donates from the Support page, sees the published thank-you state and downloads the receipt PDF from their account.

Catalog prices per currency
Ticket and supporter tier prices in EUR, GBP, USD and JPY come from the Kill Bill catalog in exact minor units and display in the published format, including whole yen.

Joining a supporter plan
Joining creates a Kill Bill subscription that is invoiced and paid at the catalog price for the chosen tier and currency before the app reports success, and the Kill Bill account's currency is then fixed for every later payment, as qualified in Business rules.

Live plan price
In the Supporter plan dialog the price updates in place and is announced as the visitor switches tier or currency.

Plan dialog survives page timers
The Supporter plan dialog, its chosen tier and its unsaved currency stay as the supporter left them while narration plays and plates cross-fade, and reopening it during its closing animation keeps it open.

Immediate upgrade
An upgrade takes effect at once in Kill Bill, charges the prorated amount Kill Bill invoices, and shows the new tier only after Kill Bill confirms it.

Pending downgrade and cancellation
A downgrade or cancellation is scheduled in Kill Bill for the end of the paid term, shows the current tier marked Pending change with Kill Bill's date, and can be undone while pending.

Membership change journey
A supporter joins, upgrades, schedules a downgrade, sees it pending on their account and undoes it, all in the browser.

Declined membership charge leaves the membership overdue
A declined upgrade charge answers 402, leaves the upgrade applied in Kill Bill with its invoice unpaid, shows the membership Overdue on the new tier and sends the first dunning email, while a declined join leaves no active subscription.

Dunning after a declined charge
After a declined membership charge the server retries with the card on file on the published schedule set by DUNNING_RETRY_SECONDS, sends a reminder after each failed retry, and cancels the subscription in Kill Bill after the third failure.

Overdue charge settles once
However many manual retries, automatic retries, replays and server instances act on one overdue charge at once, it settles with exactly one Kill Bill payment, one ledger row, one receipt and one PDF, and every losing attempt gets the published 409.

Overdue supporter journey
A supporter whose upgrade charge is declined sees Overdue on their account, updates their card, retries the payment and returns to Active with one receipt.

Editorial lifecycle
Chapters and timeline events move only along the published lifecycle, with role checks and the published rejection for each illegal move.

Scheduled publishing by server clock
A scheduled item goes live within the delay given in Business rules after its publish time by the server clock, exactly once even with several server instances on one database, and never by the browser clock.

Curator notices
Sending an item to review emails the lead curator, and withdrawing an item emails its owner, exactly once each.

Media uploads with transcripts
Curators upload images, scans and narration audio to MinIO within the published size and type limits, narration requires a transcript, and completion is announced through a polite live region.

Curator journey
A curator drafts a timeline event in an empty chapter and sends it to review, the lead curator schedules it, and visitors see it on the timeline once it goes live.

Refunds capped and confirmed
A manager's refund never exceeds the order's remaining settled amount, enters the ledger only after Kill Bill confirms it, and sends one refund email.

Session cancellation refunds every ticket
Cancelling a guided session refunds every booking in full through Kill Bill, records each refund, and sends one cancellation email per booking.

Kill Bill and MinIO outages
When Kill Bill or MinIO is unreachable, including from boot, the app still starts and serves the exhibition, and payments, receipts and media answer 503 with the published copy and nothing charged or recorded, as qualified in Server boundary.

Box-office journey
A manager creates a session, refunds part of an order, cancels a session, and sees the ledger and the staff action record update.

Reconciliation per currency
For a month in Lisbon time, the reconciliation report compares ledger and Kill Bill net totals per currency in exact minor units and flags any difference.

Effective-dated price change
A tier price change is scheduled from a future Lisbon date, is shown on the plan dialog and the Support page, changes nothing anyone is charged before that date, and sets the next payment shown to each existing member as stated in Business rules.

Staff action record
Every staff action and every automatic publication appends exactly one row to an append-only record that managers and the lead curator can list, even with several server instances on one database.

Health endpoint and run manifest
The app installs, builds and serves from the run manifest, binds the published port, and answers the health check.

Server boundary
The server enforces same-origin writes, body-size and content-type limits and the single error shape, and never serves source files or credentials.

Reduced motion stops every loop
Under reduced motion or with the Motion switch off, every loop stops, every sequence shows its end state at once, and every function stays available.

Credentials from the environment
Every service URL and credential is read from the environment at start, never hard-coded, and never sent to the browser.

Nocturnal archival look
Every screen uses the near-black ground, hairline-ruled museum cards with catalogue numbers, the serif display type, and a single signal-orange accent that marks only active or resolved state.

Procedural scenes and real media
Scenes are built from procedural 3D geometry in code, narration is real audio with transcripts, receipts are generated PDFs, and exhibit results are computed from the seed rather than looked up.

Accounts are scoped to each request
Every /api/me read and write answers for, and writes as, only the user of that request's own session cookie, under any interleaving of concurrent requests from different users.

Donations survive double submits and lost replies
Duplicate Donate submissions with the same key, whether concurrent or after a lost reply, make one donation with one receipt number, and the Donate form reuses its key for unchanged values, as qualified in API and Interactions.

One winner for simultaneous plan actions
Simultaneous membership actions for one supporter, across server instances, are judged against the membership state at commit, so exactly one is placed in Kill Bill and each other gets the published 409.

Lisbon wall-clock entry across clock changes
Publish-at and session start entries are read as Lisbon wall-clock time on any device, a repeated hour means its first occurrence, and a skipped hour shows the published field error and sends nothing.

Refund totals and seats stay consistent under concurrency
Simultaneous refunds on one order never together exceed its settled amount, and an order's refunded total and a session's seats left always match their recomputed values, under any interleaving of refunds, bookings and cancellation.

Latest search input wins
Timeline results and the search count always match the current search text and chapter filter, even when a reply for earlier input arrives last.

Timeline search lives in the address
The timeline's search text and chapter filter are held in the page address, so reloading or sharing it restores the same query, filter and results, as qualified in Interactions.

Closed panels are unavailable
Closed Menu and Chapters sheets, the collapsed transcript and closed or closing dialogs have nothing visible, reachable by Tab or in the accessibility tree, at every viewport.

Session times are Lisbon on every device
Session cards, the booking confirmation, the ticket email and the PDF show the server's Lisbon start time whatever the device's zone or clock, including across a Lisbon clock change.
/app/run.json is a JSON object with exactly the string keys _schema (value run-manifest-v1), install, build and serve.

THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package, with its name, version and licence, plus the three fonts; shipped packages means the production dependency tree reported by npm ls --omit=dev --all --json.
Every shipped package (the same production dependency tree) is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD, Zlib, CC0-1.0 or OFL-1.1.
The app uses no datastore beyond PostgreSQL, PocketBase and MinIO: no SQLite, Redis, embedded key-value store, or JSON files used as a database.
Instrument Serif, Inter Tight and JetBrains Mono are served from the app under the OFL, with no font or script CDN.
The provided service definitions and their credentials are used unchanged.
At runtime, neither server nor browser makes network requests to hosts other than the app origin and the provided services (no analytics, CDNs or remote assets).
Application source for the server and the browser is written in TypeScript.
